scope: Theorem 11 of the manuscript “Snaky in 21 Maker moves” (preprints/Snaky-in-21-Maker-moves-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 187 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e5ce107fdc4ec77f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is one ordinary Maker policy on the initially empty infinite square board that completes an allowed copy of S within 35 actual Maker claims against every legal Breaker play. Equivalently, after extending a won position by fresh moves if necessary, its 35th Maker set contains a target whenever the first 34 Breaker replies are legal. No 35th Breaker reply is required.
